backend/servers/reality-server/src/handlers/inquiries/mod.rs:262-281 is_valid_phone mixes byte-length (`cleaned.len()` in the 9..=15 gate) with char-oriented validation (`.chars().all(is_ascii_digit)`); the two units can disagree on multi-byte payloads.

The fork-claimed PANIC on `cleaned[1..]` does NOT reproduce under static re-reading: the leading-char filter at line 275 admits only `+` or an ASCII digit (both 1-byte UTF-8), so byte 1 is always at a char boundary and the slice is safe.

Real issues that remain: (a) length gate is byte-based, not char-based — a multi-byte payload with 9 bytes but 3 chars passes the lower bound but fails the per-char digit check (returns false — benign but surprising); (b) no unit tests for `is_valid_phone` anywhere under backend/servers/reality-server/; (c) reached from 3 unauth public POSTs (`send_contact_message`, `request_viewing`, listing-report) so the test-gap matters.

Suggested fix: switch length gate to `cleaned.chars().count()` and add 3 unit tests (`+` prefix / digit prefix / unicode non-digit rejection). No security fix needed — the function is already correct on hostile input, just under-tested and byte-vs-char-confused.
